additions.reason: The Rebbe opens the Torah by establishing that the correct response to enemies is 'bechina afar' — being like dust. This is explicitly called a bechina: 'al yedei bechina afar, bechina ve-nafshi ke-afar.' The afar concept is a positive counterstrategy that neutralizes the enemy (like filling in the tunnel). In the context of Shabbat, the Rebbe also uses earth as a healing metaphor (all medicines come from the earth). The concept of afar appears to function in the spiritual-structural domain adjacent to Package 1 (the walking/Shabbat cluster), as the humble posture that repairs the shortened steps.
additions.source_quote: רַק אַדְּרַבָּא, רָאוּי לָדוּן אוֹתָם לְכַף זְכוּת, וְלַעֲשׂוֹת לָהֶם כָּל הַטּוֹבוֹת, בְּחִינוֹת: וְנַפְשִׁי כְּעָפָר לַכֹּל תִּהְיֶה

additions.reason: The Rebbe explicitly names temura (inversion/substitution) as the defining quality of the sitra achra: 'ha-sitra achra she-hi nikret temura, ki temurat chokhmah — ivelet, temurat chayyim,' etc. Temura is the formal name for the sitra achra's nature as the inversion of all holy qualities. It belongs in Package 3 as the conceptual name for what tomar in sitra achra IS.
additions.source_quote: נִקְרָא תָּמָר, לְשׁוֹן תְּמוּרָה, הַיְנוּ הַסִּטְרָא אָחֳרָא שֶׁהִיא נִקְרֵאת תְּמוּרָה, כִּי תְּמוּרַת חָכְמָה – אִוֶּלֶת

additions.reason: The Rebbe explicitly states that the sitra achra and its root are machloket, and the shaor is 'klalut ve-tokef ha-dinim.' The dinim (harsh judgments) are the substance of the evil force. The Torah discusses sweetening dinim at their root (shoresh). Dinim as a concept is a bechina of the sitra achra's concentrated force.
additions.source_quote: כִּי שְׂאוֹר הוּא כְּלָלוּת וְתֹקֶף הַדִּינִים, כִּי הוּא בְּחִינַת אֱלֹקִים בְּרִבּוּעַ וּבְמִלּוּי

additions.reason: The Rebbe says 'kol mitzvah hi komah shlemah' and describes mitzvot as having feet (raglayim) from which the sitra achra suckles during the week, but on Shabbat the feet are returned to holiness and the mitzvah begins to walk before God. The mitzvah's walking IS the domain of Package 1 (pesi'ot, raglayim, derekh kevushah). The Rebbe explicitly uses bechina language: 'zeh bechina: tzedek lefanav yehalekh' — the mitzvah walking is tzedek, which is bechina of pesi'ot.
additions.source_quote: כָּל מִצְוָה הִיא קוֹמָה שְׁלֵמָה... וּבְשַׁבָּת עוֹלִין הָרַגְלִין מִן הַקְּלִפּוֹת... וַאֲזַי מַתְחֶלֶת לֵילֵךְ לִפְנֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

additions.reason: The Rebbe explicitly equates tzedek with mitzvot through bechina language: 'tzedek, haynu ha-mitzvot, kema she-katuv: kol mitzvotekha tzedek.' And then 'tzedek lefanav yehalekh' — the mitzvah walking before God. Tzedek is a bechina of the mitzvah in motion, which belongs to Package 1's domain of walking/pesi'ot.
additions.source_quote: וְזֶה בְּחִינוֹת: צֶדֶק לְפָנָיו יְהַלֵּךְ. צֶדֶק, הַיְנוּ הַמִּצְווֹת

additions.reason: The Rebbe says eretz Yisrael is the primary land; all other lands receive from its essence (tamtzit). Eretz Yisrael when at peace is called simply 'eretz' — 'eretz natna yevulah' — giving its produce fully. This is the positive state that is bechina of shalom/healing. Eretz Yisrael in its pure state = eretz natna yevulah = shalom = Package 4.
additions.source_quote: וְעִקָּר הוּא אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, כִּי כָּל הָאֲרָצוֹת מְקַבְּלִין מִתַּמְצִית אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל

additions.reason: The Torah distinguishes between machloket of tzaddikim (holy, for good) and machloket of reshaim (pure evil, the actual sitra achra). The text explicitly contrasts them. Machloket of reshaim is the direct expression of the sitra achra and belongs in Package 3.
additions.source_quote: וְכָל זֶה כְּשֶׁהַחוֹלְקִים הֵם רְשָׁעִים, אֲבָל כְּשֶׁחוֹלְקִים עָלָיו צַדִּיקִים, בְּוַדַּאי כַּוָּנָתָם הוּא רַק לְטוֹבָה

additions.reason: The Rebbe explicitly calls machloket of tzaddikim a 'great good' (tova gedola) — it is the machloket bi-kedushah (holy conflict) that sweetens the judgments at their root (in the shoresh). It is a bechina of ha-matak ha-dinim. Machloket of tzaddikim causes 'tzaddik ka-tamar yifrach' — it belongs in Package 2 as the holy process that produces the tamar bi-kedushah flourishing.
additions.source_quote: מַחֲלֹקֶת שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים הִיא טוֹבָה גְּדוֹלָה... עַל יְדֵי מַחֲלֹקֶת שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים... נִמְתָּקִים הַדִּינִים בְּשָׁרְשָׁן

analysis_notes.mirror_structure_note: Package 2 (tamar bi-kedushah / sweetening of judgments) is the exact good mirror of Package 3 (tamar in sitra achra / concentrated dinim). Package 4 (shalom / healing / earth giving produce) is the good mirror of the Canaan/poverty sub-cluster within Package 3. Package 1 straddles both poles: chilul Shabbat = the evil/degraded state; Shabbat itself (שבת/אשתו ראשונה) = the holy entity whose loss causes the degradation. The Torah's argument is: machloket of tzaddikim sweetens dinim (Pkg2 defeats Pkg3 evil) → shalom/healing follows (Pkg4) → the walking/Shabbat is repaired by Shabbat eating (eitza chain within and beyond Pkg1).
